parts.text: When n is even there is no middle square so we use a different method to make a magic square. • Draw the two diagonals on the 4 by 4 square. • Put the smallest integer in the top left square. • Go from left to right , but only write the integers in the squares where there is part of a diagonal. • Starting with the bottom row write the remaining integers, in order, from right to left in the empty squares.

content.tex: When \(n\) is even there is no middle square so we use a different method to make a magic square.

\(\bullet\) Draw the two diagonals on the 4 by 4 square. \(\bullet\) Put the smallest integer in the top left square. \(\bullet\) Go from left to right, but only write the integers in the squares where there is part of a diagonal.
\(\bullet\) Starting with the bottom row write the remaining integers, in order, from right to left in the empty squares.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Use this method to complete the 4 by 4 magic square with the consecutive integers k to k 15 + . There is an extra grid for working. [2]
